t: Nothing of Carlton House survives here. It was a grand mansion facing Pall Mall, with gardens running down to St James's Park, and it was best known as the town home of the Prince Regent, later George IV. Carlton House Terrace now stands on the site. The house mattered to the whole shape of this part of London, because Lower Regent Street and Waterloo Place were laid out as the approach to its front door, and John Nash's route to Regent's Park grew from that. Henry Holland designed it. Princess Charlotte, the Prince's only child, was born here.
